symbols.name: Ubi
symbols.def: \(U_{\leftrightarrow}=\{\{u,v\}:u,v\in V\}\), where \(\{u,v\}\) is unordered and \(u=v\) denotes a bidirected loop

symbols.name: InternalBi
symbols.role: exact within-SCC bidirected edges including loops

definitions.name: Two-copy lift
definitions.construction: For \(G\), each directed edge \(u\to v\), including \(u=v\), gives \(u_0\to v_0\), \(u_0\to v_1\), and \(u_1\to v_1\). Each unordered bidirected edge \(\{u,v\}\), including \(u=v\), gives \(u_p\leftrightarrow v_q\) for every \(p,q\in\{0,1\}\). Thus a bidirected loop \(\{u,u\}\) gives the three distinct unordered lifted edges \(\{u_0,u_0\}\), \(\{u_0,u_1\}\), and \(\{u_1,u_1\}\); the index choices \((0,1)\) and \((1,0)\) name the same cross-copy edge.

definitions.name: E-model
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal I_E(G)=\{(A,B,C):\text{no \(\sigma\)-open walk given \(D(B,C)\) in \(\operatorname{Lift}(G)\) joins \(A_0\) to \(B_1\)}\}\).

definitions.name: Admissible edges
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Adm}(G)=\{e\in(U_{\to}\cup U_{\leftrightarrow})\setminus E(G):\Sigma_E(G+e)=\Sigma_E(G)\}\), where candidates include directed loops and unordered bidirected loops.

definitions.name: Union candidate
definitions.construction: \(G^\star=(V,\bigcup_{H\equiv_E G}E^{\to}(H),\bigcup_{H\equiv_E G}E^{\leftrightarrow}(H))\), with componentwise union over \(U_{\to}\) and \(U_{\leftrightarrow}\), including directed and bidirected loops.

definitions.name: Compelled edges
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Comp}(G)=\bigcap\{E^{\to}(H)\cup E^{\leftrightarrow}(H):H\in\mathfrak D(V),H\equiv_E G\}\), where either kind of loop may be compelled.

definitions.name: Directed SCC partition
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{SCC}(G)=\{S\subseteq V:S\neq\varnothing,\ S\text{ is a maximal strongly connected set in }(V,E^{\to}(G))\}\), using reflexive directed reachability.

definitions.name: Incoming-to-SCC support
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{In}_{\mathrm{SCC}}(G)=\{(u,S):S\in\operatorname{SCC}(G),\ u\in V\setminus S,\ \exists v\in S\text{ with }(u,v)\in E^{\to}(G)\}\).

definitions.name: Cross-SCC bidirected support
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Cross}_{\leftrightarrow}(G)=\{\{S,T\}:S,T\in\operatorname{SCC}(G),\ S\neq T,\ \exists u\in S,\exists v\in T\text{ with }\{u,v\}\in E^{\leftrightarrow}(G)\}\).

definitions.name: Internal bidirected support
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Int}_{\leftrightarrow}(G)=\{\{u,v\}\in E^{\leftrightarrow}(G):\exists S\in\operatorname{SCC}(G)\text{ with }u,v\in S\}\); this exact set includes every present bidirected loop \(\{u,u\}\).

definitions.name: Fixed-profile saturation
definitions.construction: Define \(\Gamma(G)=(V,E^{\to}_{\Gamma}(G),E^{\leftrightarrow}_{\Gamma}(G))\) uniquely by \(E^{\to}_{\Gamma}(G)=E^{\to}(G)\cup\{(u,v)\in U_{\to}:\exists S\in\operatorname{SCC}(G)\text{ such that }v\in S\text{ and }[(u\in S\land |S|\ge2)\lor (u,S)\in\operatorname{In}_{\mathrm{SCC}}(G)]\}\) and \(E^{\leftrightarrow}_{\Gamma}(G)=E^{\leftrightarrow}(G)\cup\{\{u,v\}\in U_{\leftrightarrow}:\exists S,T\in\operatorname{SCC}(G),\ S\neq T,\ u\in S,\ v\in T,\ \{S,T\}\in\operatorname{Cross}_{\leftrightarrow}(G)\}\). Hence internal bidirected edges, including bidirected loops, and directed-loop status on singleton SCCs are retained exactly, while every non-singleton SCC receives all directed loops.

definitions.name: Contextual replacement handle
definitions.construction: \(R\) starts from the first new lifted-edge occurrence on a shortest newly open walk and records minimal directed certificates for each collider newly activated or conditioned tail newly internal; equivalence with \(H\) supplies singleton witnesses to splice with identical endpoint marks, copy indices, and conditioning \(D(B,C)\). For a bidirected-loop candidate \(e=\{u,u\}\), the occurrence record distinguishes the two copywise lifted loops from the cross-copy lifted edge and records the traversal orientation of the cross-copy occurrence.

definitions.name: Finite recovery
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Alg}_E\) queries all \(a,b\in V\) and \(C\subseteq V\setminus\{a\}\), enumerates the finite class \(\mathfrak D(V)\) with candidate set \(U_{\to}\cup U_{\leftrightarrow}\), unions both edge types over all matching DMGs, and marks any directed edge, bidirected edge, directed loop, or bidirected loop compelled exactly when deleting it changes the signature.

statements.statement: For every \(G\) and \(A,B,C\subseteq V\), \((A,B,C)\in\mathcal I_E(G)\) iff every \((\{a\},\{b\},C)\in\mathcal I_E(G)\), including diagonal queries and \(B\cap C\neq\varnothing\).
statements.justification: It makes the full asymmetric model a finite singleton-oracle object.
statements.gap: Right composition must handle the target-dependent conditioning set.
statements.consumer: The recovery map stores only singleton answers.

statements.statement: If \(G\subseteq H\), then \(\mathcal I_E(H)\subseteq\mathcal I_E(G)\); hence \(G\subseteq K\subseteq H\) and \(G\equiv_E H\) imply \(K\equiv_E G\).
statements.justification: This interval property converts transfer into union closure.
statements.gap: The check must include ancestry enlargement and SCC merging.
statements.consumer: Saturation and deletion tests avoid intermediate retesting.

statements.statement: For every \(G\in\mathfrak D(V)\), the edgewise formulas define a unique finite \(\Gamma(G)\in\mathfrak D(V)\), and \(\operatorname{Prof}(\Gamma(G))=\operatorname{Prof}(G)\). In particular, no new internal bidirected edge or bidirected loop is inserted, every present bidirected loop remains present, and the directed-loop status of every singleton SCC is unchanged.
statements.justification: It verifies that simultaneous saturation is a uniquely specified operation on the full finite-DMG universe.
statements.gap: A simultaneous mixed saturation needs an invariant profile theorem for every inserted edge, including directed-loop and bidirected-loop cases.
statements.consumer: The fixed-profile theorem can quantify over one exact realizable family and one well-defined greatest member.

statements.statement: For every \(G\in\mathfrak D(V)\), every \(H\in\mathfrak F_G\) satisfies \(\mathcal I_E(H)=\mathcal I_E(G)\), the finite family \(\mathfrak F_G\) is closed under componentwise directed-and-bidirected edge union, and \(\Gamma(G)\in\mathfrak F_G\) is its unique greatest member with \(\mathcal I_E(\Gamma(G))=\mathcal I_E(G)\). These conclusions retain all internal bidirected edges and bidirected loops exactly while completing only occupied cross-SCC bidirected rectangles.
statements.justification: It isolates the maximal regime where direct substitution works.
statements.gap: Published local moves are not packaged as simultaneous mixed saturation.
statements.consumer: It supplies base cases and reduction tests for transfer.

statements.statement: Construct \(R\) whenever \(G\equiv_E H\) and \(e\in E(H)\setminus E(G)\), transforming every \(\sigma\)-open walk in \(\operatorname{Lift}(G+e)\) given \(D(B,C)\) into one in \(\operatorname{Lift}(G)\) with the same endpoint copies and conditioning. The construction must cover SCC-changing arrows, directed self-loops, the two copywise and one cross-copy lifted edges generated by a bidirected loop, collider activation, SCC-tail changes, and first bidirected connections outside occupied SCC rectangles.
statements.justification: This is the genuinely open proof mechanism.
statements.gap: Only \(\mu\)-splicing and fixed-profile E-replacements are published.
statements.consumer: It yields unrestricted transfer and certificates for optional edges.

statements.statement: For all \(G\equiv_E H\) and \(e\in E(H)\setminus E(G)\), \(G+e\equiv_E G\) for every \(e\in U_{\to}\cup U_{\leftrightarrow}\). This includes SCC-changing arrows, directed self-loops, unordered bidirected loops \(\{u,u\}\), arbitrary directed cycles, and bidirected additions outside occupied SCC rectangles.
statements.justification: This local theorem resolves the global conjecture by iteration.
statements.gap: No published E-result covers these unrestricted regimes.
statements.consumer: Equivalent representatives become connected by safe edge additions.

statements.statement: Every E-equivalence class in \(\mathfrak D(V)\) is closed under componentwise binary union of directed and unordered bidirected edges, including both kinds of loops; \(G^\star\equiv_E G\) is its unique greatest member. This strictly extends Manten et al.'s directed theorem to the full finite-DMG class and settles their all-DMG conjecture.
statements.justification: It identifies one canonical mixed graph from the E-model.
statements.gap: The source proves only the directed theorem and four-node mixed evidence.
statements.consumer: Latent cyclic path-space discovery gains a unique maximally informative target.

statements.statement: \(G+\operatorname{Adm}(G)=G^\star\) and \(\mathcal I_E(G+\operatorname{Adm}(G))=\mathcal I_E(G)\), where \(\operatorname{Adm}(G)\) ranges over all absent directed edges and unordered bidirected edges, including both loop types, even when additions jointly change SCCs and create previously unoccupied bidirected rectangles.
statements.justification: It turns global closure into edgewise saturation.
statements.gap: Individual safety does not generally imply joint safety.
statements.consumer: An oracle algorithm tests only one-edge additions.

statements.statement: From \(Q=n^2 2^{n-1}\) nontrivial oracle answers, \(\operatorname{Alg}_E\) returns \((G^\star,\operatorname{Comp}(G))\) over the full candidate universe \(U_{\to}\cup U_{\leftrightarrow}\); for every directed edge, bidirected edge, directed loop, or bidirected loop \(e\in E(G^\star)\), \(e\in\operatorname{Comp}(G)\) iff \(\Sigma_E(G^\star-e)\neq\Sigma_E(G^\star)\).
statements.justification: It converts existence into exact structure identification.
statements.gap: Greatest-plus-compelled recovery exists for \(\mu\), not mixed E-separation.
statements.consumer: Discovery reports compelled, optional, and impossible process mechanisms.

statements.statement: If \(E^{\leftrightarrow}(G)=\varnothing\), \(G^\star\) is exactly the directed greatest representative of Manten et al.
statements.justification: This is the required standard-case sanity check.
statements.gap: It is a reduction, not a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: Fully observed E-discovery is recovered unchanged.

sampling_model.design: Exact finite E-separation oracle; no random sampling enters the identification theorem.
sampling_model.units: Fixed finite labeled vertices \(V\) and the full finite-DMG universe with directed and unordered bidirected loops.
sampling_model.treatment: No designated treatment; the target is causal structure.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; estimating oracle answers is downstream.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Greatest E-representatives are proved for directed graphs and conjectured for DMGs.
Legitimate mark changes connect equivalent directed MAGs.
Cyclic FCI is complete for several \(\sigma\)-features.
Integer programming gives globally optimal learning for supported criteria.
A canonical projection exists for separable graphs.

tldr: E-separation gives an asymmetric Markov model for cyclic path systems, but latent coordinates introduce bidirected edges and defeat the directed canonical-graph proof. On the full finite-DMG universe, where unordered bidirected pairs may be loops, unrestricted single-edge transfer yields binary-union closure, a unique greatest representative, simultaneous admissible-edge saturation, and singleton-oracle recovery of greatest and compelled edges. A precisely defined fixed mixed SCC-profile family supplies a greatest member by edgewise saturation while retaining internal bidirected loops; the open content is contextual lifted-walk replacement for SCC changes, collider activation, directed loops, bidirected loops, and first cross-SCC bidirected connections.

project_justification.gap: The 2025 source proves only the directed greatest theorem and restricted mixed saturation; no theorem covers the cited finite-DMG universe with unordered bidirected loops, SCC-merging arrows, or first cross-SCC bidirected connections.
project_justification.niche: Latent cyclic path-space discovery lacks a canonical E-equivalence representative and a formally specified mixed SCC-profile saturation on that full edge universe.
project_justification.fill: Define the profile edgewise, prove its unique finite saturation, and establish unrestricted transfer on the published DMG class to derive union closure, simultaneous admissible-edge saturation, and recovery, all including directed and bidirected loops.

related_work: Manten et al. (2025) define the finite directed mixed setting used here, including unordered bidirected pairs with coincident endpoints, prove the directed greatest theorem, give restricted mixed replacements, and state the all-DMG conjecture resolved by Theorem 2. The fixed-profile proposition isolates their replacement regime through the exact tuple consisting of the directed SCC partition, incoming-to-SCC support, occupied cross-SCC bidirected support, exact internal bidirected support including loops, and singleton-SCC directed-loop support. Mogensen and Hansen (2020) supply the closest \(\mu\)-walk proof architecture, not an E-result. Zhang and Spirtes (2005) inform local-change induction under ancestral restrictions. Mooij and Claassen (2020) recover \(\sigma\)-features rather than an E-greatest graph. Claassen and Mooij (2023) treat cyclic directed \(d\)-equivalence. Kook and Mogensen (2026) give optimization encodings without E-union closure. Meek and Sadeghi (2026) give a canonical projection for a different vertex-separation model.
technical_internal_limitation: The completed five-vertex falsification gate exhausted \(384{,}168\) bases with at most five edges in the \(35\)-edge subuniverse that excludes bidirected loops. It performed \(12{,}360{,}756\) signature checks, found \(708{,}990\) safe additions and \(254{,}865\) signatures, merged \(94{,}838\) equal-signature collisions, and found no simultaneous or class-union failure. The full five-vertex universe has \(40\) possible edges and \(\sum_{k=0}^{5}\binom{40}{k}=760{,}099\) such sparse bases, so the existing computation does not test bidirected-loop additions and is not the full loop-inclusive early kill gate. All computation is evidence, not a finite obstruction bound or proof.
honest_scope: Contextual replacement and unrestricted transfer remain open on the full finite-DMG class, including bidirected loops. Composition, antitonicity, well-defined profile saturation, and fixed-profile E-equivalence are supporting claims. The existing exhaustive sparse check omits bidirected loops. Recovery assumes an exact oracle and makes no faithfulness or finite-sample claim. When all bidirected edges, including bidirected loops, are absent, the result must reduce exactly to Manten et al.'s directed theorem.

novelty_justification: Manten et al. (2025) prove the greatest theorem for directed graphs and permit a mixed bidirected addition only when the endpoint SCCs already share a bidirected edge. Their finite-DMG universe permits unordered bidirected pairs with coincident endpoints. The proposed theorem covers SCC-merging arrows, directed self-loops, unordered bidirected loops, first cross-SCC bidirected edges, and internal bidirected additions. Mogensen and Hansen (2020) prove the analogous \(\mu\)-result, but E-separation has a two-copy lift and target-dependent conditioning. The kernel therefore settles the published conjecture on its stated loop-inclusive class.
